From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 04 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: InferAPI cutover sync: ticketing, comms & exception intake

Team —

We need to lock decisions for the InferAPI default-model cutover (consolidation of model-variant family v2 -> v1-compat) and get a single source of truth for tickets, comms, and exception intake. This will touch Hosted API defaults, Dedicated routing, and the Private deployment docs. High-level asks:

- Product: confirm cutover policy (force-default switch vs. opt-in) and the public deprecation window length.
- Engineering: confirm blackout windows, rollback/hotswap feasibility, and whether a compatibility shim can buy us a longer tail.
- CS/Support: how we intake and triage customer exception requests (fields, SLA to respond, templates).

Preliminary timeline (please comment with constraints):
- May 8: decide policy (force vs opt-in) and list of customers requiring exceptions
- May 15: open public notice + release notes / sample migration guide
- May 30: staged cutover (regions: us-east -> eu-west -> apac) with canary in us-east-1

I'm attaching a draft cutover ticket template for intake. Please respond with owners + any firm blocking constraints by EOD May 8. If you need earlier signoffs for your teams, flag that in reply.

Playbook links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CutoverRunbookPreview
Jira epic: INFER-7421

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Program Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 04 May 2029 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: InferAPI cutover sync: ticketing, comms & exception intake

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear ask. A few product/roadmap clarifications from my side:

1) Canary approach: we should gate the default switch behind a feature flag per region and enable a 48h canary window (us-east-1) where latency and unit-cost metrics are monitored. If p50 latency regresses >12% or token-error rate >0.4% we rollback automatically.

2) Migration docs: I will draft a migration guide seed that includes common SDK changes + example curl payloads. ETA for first draft: May 11.

3) Opt-in vs forced: I'd like to propose a hybrid: make v2 the default for new API keys immediately, but opt existing keys into a 60-day migration window unless they explicitly request immediate cutover. This reduces churn while giving power users a shorter path. Need confirmation if this meets product goals.

Questions for Engineering: can we attach a per-key opt-in flag easily in Dedicated routing? And can we surface a migration-needed header for affected responses?

I'll own the public comms messaging (blog + release notes) once we align.

—Karthik
Product Manager

Priyom / Karthik —

From a CS/Support perspective we need a simple exception intake flow and a firm SLA for initial response. Operational asks:

- Intake form fields: customer name, account id, contact person, API key(s), reason for exception, requested end date, business impact (high/med/low), required mitigation steps.
- SLA: acknowledge within 24 hours, decision within 5 business days for standard requests.
- For top-tier customers (Enterprise tier) we need a faster lane (48h decision) and a clear list of compensatory options (credits, extended support).

We already have one pilot that will request extended window: Acme Corp (John Li). They're running a legacy offline batch integration that expects the older variant. John has asked for a 120-day exception window if we can't provide a compatibility shim. I've attached their intake PDF.

Also: please confirm whether exceptions will be staged via Jira or a dedicated exceptions tracker. Suggestion: a central spreadsheet during the early phase, then move to a Jira board once the list stabilizes.

Ben
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Technical constraints and proposals from Platform:

- Blackout windows: we prefer to avoid major database schema changes within 48h of a region maintenance window. Please flag any proposed changes so we can schedule around the next three maintenance windows (us-east-1: May 20-21, eu-west-1: May 26).

- Shim: we can provide a light-weight compatibility shim that rewrites specific request headers and provides KV-based fallback to the older tokenization for ~90% of calls. That approach will add ~6% CPU cost on the serving path and complicate observability slightly. If the pilot customers accept a 90-day exception, I think we can avoid shipped shims for everyone.

- Rollback/hotswap: in practice we can hot-swap the default variant within a 15-minute window assuming no schema changes and following the checklist I attached. Post-cutover we should keep a 72h watch and an automated sanity check job that validates end-to-end responses for the top 20 customers.

Decision deadline: we need a clear product policy by EOD May 8 to schedule the engineering tasks for the week of May 13.

Irene
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good alignment so far. Summary and owners: 

- Product policy: Karthik proposed hybrid opt-in (new keys -> v2 default; existing keys get 60-day migration window). Action: Karthik to confirm final wording and share the public notice draft by May 11 (owner: Karthik).

- Engineering: Irene to validate shim cost tradeoffs and confirm ability to spin a per-key opt-in flag for Dedicated routing. Action: send final feasibility note by May 8 (owner: Irene).

- CS/Exceptions: Ben to take Acme request, open intake row in central spreadsheet, and propose SLA/decision templates. Action: Ben to circulate spreadsheet and initial triage of current requests by May 7 (owner: Ben).

- Runbook & testing: I'll schedule a tabletop runbook rehearsal week of May 20 and request a canary window for us-east-1 May 30 -> June 1. Action: Priyom to create Jira epic INFER-7421 and schedule rehearsal (owner: Priyom).

Open decisions needing input:
- Final length of migration window for existing keys (60 vs 90 days) — product decision by May 8.
- Whether we accept 120-day exceptions for Acme as a precedent — ops + leadership signoff if yes.

If no further constraints, I'll convert the ticket template into the exceptions sheet and create the Jira epic tonight. We'll run a short sync Monday to confirm owners — 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Priyom
Program Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
